status: RC — rc10 adds `transplayer snapshot-seed` (B): a one-shot seed that rotates fresh Chrome profiles to capture a clean image-results page for all 13 queries into the shared cache, reaching the hard queries that even rc9's fresh display profiles can't on a flagged IP (new-session grace window; capture clean back-to-back, rotate on gate; bounded by 20 profiles). Reuses rc9's isCleanResults/writeSnapshot; runs safe alongside the live player (own seed-* profiles, TRANSPLAYER_SEED stops it wiping se_*). Account-login (A) to layer in via the settings GUI. rc9 hardens the snapshot cache against stale/grey content. (1) Fresh display profiles each run: the controller removes the persistent se_* chrome profiles at startup (keeping the snapshots/ cache) so every run starts in Google's new-session grace window and the post-boot warm-up captures today's clean page for all 13 queries, instead of a flagged long-lived profile that can never re-capture its 'hard' queries and keeps serving a days-old snapshot. (2) Positive capture gate: a page is cached only when it has >=25 image-result thumbnails (real pages carry 200+, a grey/reCAPTCHA page ~0), failing closed on gated/error, so a masked reCAPTCHA page is never captured and later served as results. NopeCHA stays disabled (it can't solve the Enterprise reCAPTCHA and re-adds on-screen bars). Still requires dash-to-dock dock-fixed=false; release gates still open
